limitations_and_boundaries: Neural operators cannot perfectly approximate the ground-truth operator when only coarse-resolution training data is provided.
Generalization of learned neural operators to unseen scenarios and conditions different from training data is challenging.

research_questions.statement: Can a hybrid approach combining training data and physics constraints at different resolutions learn the solution operator of parametric PDEs with high accuracy and zero-shot super-resolution?

provenance.text_excerpt: The resulting PINO model can accurately approximate the ground-truth solution operator for many popular PDE families and shows no degradation in accuracy even under zero-shot super-resolution, i.e., being able to predict beyond the resolution of training data.

claims.statement: PINO can accurately approximate the ground-truth solution operator for many popular PDE families and shows no degradation in accuracy even under zero-shot super-resolution.

provenance.text_excerpt: PINO is the first hybrid approach incorporating data and PDE constraints at different resolutions to learn the operator.

claims.statement: PINO is the first hybrid approach incorporating data and PDE constraints at different resolutions to learn the operator.

provenance.text_excerpt: Moreover, PINO succeeds in settings where no training data is available and only PDE constraints are imposed, while previous approaches, such as the Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), fail due to optimization challenges, e.g., in multi-scale dynamic systems such as Kolmogorov flows.

claims.statement: PINO succeeds in settings where no training data is available and only PDE constraints are imposed, while previous approaches such as PINN fail due to optimization challenges.

experiments_or_tasks: Propose physics-informed neural operators (PINO) that combine coarse-resolution training data with PDE constraints imposed at a higher resolution to learn the solution operator of parametric PDEs.

methods.name: Physics-Informed Neural Operator (PINO)
methods.protocol_description: PINO uses the Fourier neural operator (FNO) framework, which is a universal approximator for continuous operators and discretization convergent. PDE constraints are added to FNO at a higher resolution than the training data, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction of the ground-truth operator. The approach can also work without training data, using only PDE constraints.

provenance.text_excerpt: PINO achieves 0.38% relative l2 error averaged over 200 testing instances. PINN-DeepONet achieves 1.38% which is taken from Wang et al. [52] which uses the same problem setting.

claims.statement: PINO outperforms PINN-DeepONet on Burgers equation with 0.38% vs 1.38% relative L2 error.
